conclusion.launch_gate_interpretation: Admissible only if worker-execution means active computation/checkpoint/restore/native-replay/fresh-L2 payload work, not allocated idle pod lifetime. Record that definition in the frozen protocol/admission receipt.

concrete_enforcement_issue: The request/controller has no cumulative elapsed counter and does not wait for predecessor Pod deletion before the fresh Job may run. A controller crash after fresh Job creation could leave an idle predecessor Pod allocated until its absolute deadline. Thus the 14,400 cap is not provable if worker-execution includes allocated Pod/instance lifetime rather than active scientific payload execution.

deadline_margin_observed_read_only.qualification: Point-in-time source-review observation; launch remained unperformed.

serial_execution_argument: Initial computation, checkpoint and in-pod native replay share one attempt pod.
A restore cannot start until the previous writer instance is terminated.
Fresh L2 creation occurs only after the old computation and native replay are complete.
Therefore active scientific payload intervals do not overlap. The idle predecessor supervisor pod may overlap the fresh job, but it performs no scientific payload after verified transition.
smallest_no_source_change_admission_trea: Freeze an explicit definition that worker-execution elapsed counts active scientific payload/checkpoint/restore/replay/fresh-L2 intervals, excluding a verified predecessor Pod that is idle while deletion completes.
Record the actual submission timestamp and prove it is at least the grace/overlap allowance after 23:32:22Z; preserve the fixed 03:32:22Z deadline.
At admission/readback, verify no preexisting run and preserve all attempt/Pod start-finish times so additive active intervals can be recomputed.

If the approved definition instead includes allocated worker lifetime, current source is insufficient and launch should remain blocked pending an explicit cumulative counter or deletion-complete fence.

source_evidence.fact: Strict request has deadline but no additive-budget field; initial admission binds original deadline and does not reset it.
Every computation/restore pod gets activeDeadlineSeconds equal to the remaining original deadline.
Restore begins only after the exact previous EC2 writer is confirmed terminated; attempts are serial.
Supervisor checks the original deadline every loop and kills the payload process group; RPC operations are serialized.
Native replay is synchronous in the same predecessor pod and must finish before its status becomes verified.
Computation completes, replay verifies, archive/readback finishes, then benchmark phase begins.
Fresh L2 job gets remaining deadline minus 120 seconds, no retry, and succeeds only after verification/readback. Old pod deletion is asynchronous after fresh job UID is bound.
L2 job has backoffLimit=0, activeDeadlineSeconds, and 60-second termination grace.

synchronous_boundary: verify() and CRIU operations can block the supervisor loop past its next explicit deadline check. The Pod active deadline is the fallback. The fresh job reserves 120 seconds and has 60-second termination grace; the computation pod omits an explicit terminationGracePeriodSeconds and uses the Kubernetes default. The 1,396-second prelaunch slack observed at review exceeds these normal grace windows, but that slack is external admission evidence, not an encoded cumulative counter.
